text:
Jenna (CS): FYI we have an urgent customer escalation from BrightCart — their checkout flow is failing intermittently when the model calls the price_lookup tool. They hit 400s from our runtime (schema validation). Customer says it started after they added a system prompt to force terse responses.

Ravi (Eng-ML): Can you paste the failing tool call payload? 400 from our side usually means the tool response didn't match the declared schema.

Jenna (CS): Pasting redacted convo below — note system prompt + few-shot example were added by the customer. They also reported higher 95p latency since yesterday.

Jenna (CS): ```
User: "What's the total for order 4829?"
System prompt: "Always add currency metadata and short note. Use compact JSON."
Few-shot example:
  - Input: order 123
    Output: {"currency": "USD", "total": 42}
Assistant tool call -> price_lookup(args)

price_lookup response (as received by runtime):
{"total": 42, "currency": "USD", "note": "Delivered: ok", "debug_info": {"calc_steps": [1,2,3]}, "items": [{"id": "sku-1", "price": 42}]}
```

Ravi (Eng-ML): I see extra fields like debug_info and items. Our tool schema for price_lookup expects: {"total": number, "currency": string}. The runtime's schema validator rejects extra keys if strict mode is on (which it is for BrightCart). That explains the 400s.

Tom (DevEx): Where's the mismatch coming from — model output shouldn't add arbitrary keys. Could be the system prompt's "add metadata" instruction causing the model to inject note/debug_info. Also the few-shot example includes minimal keys; the model might be over-generalizing and including metadata fields.

Kevin (Support): Customer says removing the system prompt "fixes" it, but they need that prompt for other parts of their app. They asked for a workaround without removing it.

Ravi (Eng-ML): Short-term mitigation: we can add a response-sanitizer step in the runtime that strips unexpected top-level keys before schema validation when strict=true? Or run schema validation tolerant mode then map allowed keys. But that could hide bugs.

Tom (DevEx): Agreed. Also we should provide a pattern for customers: when they use system prompts that mutate the expected tool output shape, encourage explicit tool calling instructions in the tool schema docs. Eg: "When using price_lookup, output MUST only include total and currency in the tool call; extra diagnostic fields should be returned via a separate assistant message." We should add a doc snippet and a console warning when they enable strict schema + custom system prompt.

Ravi (Eng-ML): Repro steps I ran locally to replicate:
1) Spawn a chat session with model gpt-redwood-13b with system prompt that says "always include currency and a short note"
2) Add a few-shot example that includes currency only
3) Call the tool using our function-calling shim (see payload)

Request payload (simulated):
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "gpt-redwood-13b",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"Always add currency metadata and short note. Use compact JSON."},
    {"role":"user","content":"What's the total for order 4829?"},
    {"role":"assistant","content":"see examples"}
  ],
  "functions": [{"name":"price_lookup","parameters": {"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}},"required":["order_id"]}}],
  "function_call": {"name":"price_lookup"}
}
```

Ravi (Eng-ML): Mock tool implementation returned the extra fields. Schema validator (strict) returns 400 with body: {"error":"Tool response failed schema validation: unexpected keys: debug_info, items, note"}

OpsBot: Incident created: INC-2026-74 (auto) — assigned to eng-ml, priority=P1 per customer SLA.

Tom (DevEx): Suggestion for immediate customer-facing workaround: enable our "tool_response_filter" flag set to "whitelist_only" which will drop unexpected keys before validation and log the dropped keys. It preserves strict semantics but avoids hard 400s. We can roll this as a temporary console toggle.

Kevin (Support): I'll propose that to BrightCart and offer to enable the switch while they tweak prompts. Also asking them to share their few-shot examples so we can advise changes.

Ravi (Eng-ML): Long-term fixes:
- Add a runtime sanitizer that can be configured per-customer: drop extra keys OR nest extras under _meta. That way the tool receives only declared keys but we keep debugging info.
- Improve token-level docs + examples showing how system prompts can cause schema drift.
- Add a new eval in model onboarding that detects "metadata hallucination" when few-shot/system prompt likely to produce extra keys for function calls.

Tom (DevEx): I'll draft the console warning language and a docs snippet for tool authors: sample rule: "Do not request free-form metadata inside tool call outputs; use a dedicated metadata tool or assistant message instead."

Jenna (CS): Customer just responded: they can temporarily turn off the system prompt but want a permanent fix. They asked for a timeline.

Ravi (Eng-ML): For the sanitizer toggle we can do a staged rollout today as a chestnut patch — I'm estimating a few hours to enable a per-tenant filter (non-invasive). For the longer runtime nesting of extras we'll need ~2 sprints (design, QA, rollout).

Kevin (Support): Noted. I'll update the customer: temporary whitelist filter today, docs + best-practices within 48 hours, engineering plan for 2 sprints.

Tom (DevEx): One extra note — billing/latency: the customer reported 95p latency increase. That might be due to extra payload sizes if model emits large debug_info arrays. The sanitizer can also trim large unexpected fields which should improve latency and billing. Mention that to the customer as an upside.

Ravi (Eng-ML): Repro checklist I pushed to the incident: included unit test cases to assert that function outputs with extra keys either fail (strict) or get sanitized (whitelist). Also added a fuzz test that injects varying system prompts and verifies tool-call-only outputs.

Jenna (CS): Thanks all. Kevin — please post the customer's few-shot examples here when you get them. I'll keep the incident updated. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: INC-2026-74 updated: status=investigating, assignees=[Ravi (Eng-ML)]

Ravi (Eng-ML): Quick follow-up — logs show ~12% of their tool calls had extra keys since 2026-02-11 03:00 UTC, matching when they rolled the system prompt. That aligns.

Kevin (Support): Customer shared few-shot now — it's small, has a trailing comment line in the example that could be parsed as part of the assistant message. I'll sanitize and re-run with them.

Tom (DevEx): I'll add a console lint rule that detects comments/ambiguous example formatting inside few-shot examples that are used alongside function-calling tools.

Jenna (CS): Closing loop: I'll enable the whitelist filter for BrightCart now, notify the customer, and track engineering work. If anything new appears I'll update here.

Ravi (Eng-ML): Thanks — let me know if the filter reveals any edge cases (e.g., nested allowed keys). We'll be on standby.
